title: Morbilliform Drug Eruption Risk Algorithm
subtitle: Benign exanthem vs DRESS, SJS/TEN, AGEP, or vasculitis

steps.prompt: Morbilliform eruption after a plausible new medication exposure?
Consider viral exanthem, connective tissue disease, pityriasis rosea, secondary syphilis
Fever, facial edema, lymphadenopathy, mucosal erosions, skin pain, dusky targets, pustules, purpura?
SCAR evaluation: DRESS/SJS-TEN/AGEP/vasculitis labs, biopsy, urgent escalation
steps.detail: Urgently assess systemic illness and stop suspected culprit drugs as clinically appropriate. Lack of a recognized new exposure does not rule out a severe reaction or a serious non-drug mimic.

steps.prompt: Timing 1-3 weeks after medication start and patient clinically well?
CBC with differential, CMP, urinalysis, biopsy if persistent or atypical

citations.quote: StatPearls Cutaneous Adverse Drug Reaction review summarizes exanthematous eruptions and severe reaction warning signs.
StatPearls Stevens-Johnson Syndrome review describes mucosal involvement, skin pain, and systemic red flags.
